facts.raw_span: A white woman in her early 40s presented with generalized pruritus of 10-years' duration
She had no other medical history
She had been treated with topical corticosteroids with no control of the symptoms
Physical examination revealed erythematous papules, some of them crusted, and some excoriations located over the trunk and upper extremities
some scales and fissures were seen on her lower lip, sparing the surrounding skin, as well as inner mouth and upper lip
Blood test results including antinuclear antibodies and complement, along with urine porphyrin analysis were normal

The biopsy results showed spongiosis and erosions in the epidermis and a nodular lymphocyte infiltrate in the upper and mid dermis with a peripheral mantle zone surrounding a central germinal center with cells that were CD20 positive and BCL-2 negative
Phototest with a solar simulator was carried out with the immediate reading negative for UV-B, UV-A, and visible light
erythema appeared in the area irradiated with UV-A 48 hours afterwards

She had no other medical history
She had been treated with topical corticosteroids with no control of the symptoms
Physical examination revealed erythematous papules, some of them crusted, and some excoriations located over the trunk and upper extremities
some scales and fissures were seen on her lower lip, sparing the surrounding skin, as well as inner mouth and upper lip
Blood test results including antinuclear antibodies and complement, along with urine porphyrin analysis were normal

The biopsy results showed spongiosis and erosions in the epidermis and a nodular lymphocyte infiltrate in the upper and mid dermis with a peripheral mantle zone surrounding a central germinal center with cells that were CD20 positive and BCL-2 negative
Phototest with a solar simulator was carried out with the immediate reading negative for UV-B, UV-A, and visible light

concepts.why: The patient's symptoms of generalized pruritus, erythematous papules, and scales, along with the phototest results showing UV-A sensitivity, are consistent with Chronic Actinic Dermatitis.
The patient's skin biopsy results showing a nodular lymphocyte infiltrate with a peripheral mantle zone surrounding a central germinal center are consistent with Cutaneous T-Cell Lymphoma.
The patient's symptoms of generalized pruritus, erythematous papules, and excoriations are consistent with Atopic Dermatitis.
The patient's phototest results showing UV-A sensitivity and the development of erythema 48 hours after irradiation are consistent with Photosensitive Eczematous Dermatitis.

rationales.F01: Generalized pruritus is a common symptom in many dermatological conditions.
rationales.F04: Erythematous papules and excoriations are common skin manifestations in various dermatological conditions.
rationales.F07: The presence of a nodular lymphocyte infiltrate with a peripheral mantle zone surrounding a central germinal center is more indicative of Cutaneous T-Cell Lymphoma.
rationales.F09: The delayed onset of erythema after UV-A irradiation is a characteristic feature of Chronic Actinic Dermatitis and Photosensitive Eczematous Dermatitis.

frontier_selector.rationale: The patient's symptoms, including generalized pruritus, erythematous papules, and scales, along with the delayed erythema response to UV-A irradiation, are most consistent with Chronic Actinic Dermatitis, which is supported by the biopsy results showing spongiosis and erosions in the epidermis and a nodular lymphocyte infiltrate.
